_note: Landing-page audio. Three UI cues only, and no new voice.
No VO is generated on purpose. The site's spoken beat is CAIRN's startup
litany, which already exists at public/audio/vo/cairn_litany.mp3 in the
exact read the game plays at the top of every mission. Reusing it makes the
site a promise the game keeps thirty seconds later, costs no ElevenLabs
quota (the Creator plan is nearly spent), and cannot drift from the game.
Music is the shipped title theme, public/audio/music/theme_main.mp3.
Cues are mixed deliberately quiet. Website UI sound that is even slightly
too loud reads as amateur; these should be felt as texture, not heard as
sounds. Levels are peak-normalised by ffmpeg and asserted after encoding, not judged by eye.

sfx.usage: Chassis change in the showroom rail. Plays under the weight-settle.
sfx.prompt: A single heavy servo clunk followed immediately by a magnetic latch engaging. Dry industrial machinery, close-miked in a small hard room. No reverb tail, no music, no ringing, no room ambience.

sfx.usage: Rail tile hover, rate-limited to one play per 120 ms. Subliminal by design — if it is audible as a sound rather than felt as texture, it is too loud.
sfx.prompt: A very short dry electrical relay tick. Tiny, clean, almost inaudible. A single contact closing. No pitch, no ring, no reverb, no tail, no music.

sfx.usage: Section reveal on the campaign ladder and the FAQ.
sfx.prompt: A soft pneumatic latch releasing on a metal access panel, followed by a short hydraulic sigh. Dry, close, industrial. No reverb, no music, no metallic ring.

sfx.usage: Play button press, immediately before navigation to the game.
sfx.prompt: A heavy industrial power contactor closing, followed by a deep generator spinning up and holding. Dry, close-miked, mechanical and electrical. No music, no melody, no reverb wash.
